text:
acme-support: Hey team, raising an urgent escalation from Acme Payments — their checkout assistant started refusing to answer very benign return/refund questions after our rollout last night. Customer is seeing ~40% of previously OK queries returned as refusals.

jordan-cs: ugh. any idea which rollout touched them? they were on dedicated eu-west pool, right?

devon-sre: they were on dedicated-eu-west-2; can confirm a config change at 02:14 UTC that rolled quantized weights to that pool: rollout/id=canary-quant-v2, scope=dedicated-eu-west-2, pct=30 -> then 100 at 02:40.

eli-ml: thanks. can acme share an example prompt/response we can repro with? and tell us model_version from response headers (X-Model-Version) if possible.

acme-support: here's one (redacted):

User: "I accidentally selected wrong shipping address, can I get a refund and change delivery?"
Assistant: "Sorry, I can't help with that. I can't provide guidance on returns or refunds."

They captured response headers: X-Model-Version: redwood-medium-001-quant-v2, Request-Id: req_0a9f4c, Timestamp: 2026-03-14T02:58:12Z

sam-eng: that looks like overblocking. The prompt is safety-compliant. Could be safety policy model mismatch for the quantized variant.

eli-ml: initial hypothesis: quantization changed tokenization or scoring for some safety classifier heuristics, leading to false positives for 'refund'/'return' tokens. Also check fallback routing: if runtime falls back to a safety-stricter variant we might see more refusals.

devon-sre: I pulled the request logs for req_0a9f4c. runtime routed to redwood-medium-001-quant-v2, then a safety-check hook returned BLOCK at 0.87 confidence. Attached snippet from runtime trace:

```
[02:58:12Z] request:req_0a9f4c model:redwood-medium-001-quant-v2 seq_len:78
safety_hook result: label=block score=0.87 rules_matched=[policy_tokens:refund, ambiguity_marker]
kvcache_hit=false batching_slot=12
```

sam-eng: interesting — rules_matched mentions token "refund" which is surprising. That token shouldn't trigger block on its own. Could be a changed regex or misaligned embeddings used by the safety verifier.

eli-ml: can you run a quick local repro? try the exact prompt via curl using the hosted test endpoint for the same model tag. example:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \
  -H 'X-Model-Version: redwood-medium-001-quant-v2' \
  -d '{"input":"I accidentally selected wrong shipping address, can I get a refund and change delivery?","max_tokens":120}'
```

eli-ml: paste the raw assistant output and headers.

jordan-cs: acme also supplied a batch of 150 example prompts (benign support flows). They ran them before/after rollout and saw acceptance rate drop from 96% -> 57%.

devon-sre: I triggered a canary rollback for dedicated-eu-west-2 to the previous variant redwood-medium-001-fp16 at 03:10 UTC (auto rollback planned if errors >5% for 10m). Rollback currently in progress.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: rollout/id=canary-quant-v2 -> state=rollback requested by devon-sre at 2026-03-14T03:11:05Z.

acme-support: thanks—they reported things look better after 03:20 but still occasional refusals (~5%). They saved two more failing examples (req_0b12f7, req_0b12f8) where headers now show model redwood-medium-001-fp16 but assistant still refused.

sam-eng: ok residuals could be cache/safety policy mismatch. ask acme to provide full request headers + body for one of the failing req ids. also include trace id if available.

acme-support: sending that now. trace id=trace-9d4f, headers include X-Model-Version:redwood-medium-001-fp16, X-Request-Id:req_0b12f7. Body same as earlier. Response body: "I’m sorry, I can’t help with that request." No extra metadata.

eli-ml: two parallel investigations:
1) Compare safety-checker binary between quant-v2 and fp16 builds (we compiled new safety heuristics into quant build accidentally?)
2) Run our eval harness (safety/regression suite) against the deployed variant in a replica environment with acme's sample prompts.

sam-eng: I ran a quick diff of safety config: there was a change in policy_ruleset.json in the quant build pipeline — a hardened rule that marks "refund" in combination with address-change as potential fraud. That rule should have been feature-flag gated but appears enabled in the quant rollout bundle.

devon-sre: omg that explains it. who merged that? tagging @eli-ml and @sam-eng for root cause; will revert the safety config hotfix and kick another rollback if needed.

eli-ml: plan: revert config, redeploy safety verifier config to dedicated-eu-west-2, re-run acceptance tests for acme's sample set, monitor acceptance rate > 95% for 30m, then notify customer.

jordan-cs: timeline for revert?

sam-eng: I can push the config revert now to the config-service. Payload id=config-2026-03-14-revert-qualifier. Pushing in 2 mins.

deploy-bot: config push queued: payload=config-2026-03-14-revert-qualifier -> target:dedicated-eu-west-2

devon-sre: after revert I patched runtime to clear KV safety cache for that pool (kvcache.clear pool=dedicated-eu-west-2 key_prefix=safety-heuristics) to avoid stale rules.

acme-support: we ran a smoke set after 03:40 and acceptance rate is back to 98% for their batch. They want a postmortem and assurance it won't recur.

eli-ml: we'll prepare root cause notes: accidental enable of hardened 'refund+address' rule in quant build config + missing gating in CI -> produced over-refusal on production. Actions: stricter release gating for safety config changes, automated safety regression suite against representative customer flows, and require safety config changes to be behind a feature flag with canary off by default.

jordan-cs: pls include customer impact timeline and remediation steps for their SOC/engineering. I'll start the CS communicate draft.

sam-eng: adding follow-ups: add model variant labeling in response headers (we already have X-Model-Version but add X-Model-Variant-build-id) and a canary smoke test that includes a set of benign customer prompts.

devon-sre: logging note: capture safety_hook.(label,score,rules_matched) in request traces for 24h after deploy so we can spot drift faster.

acme-support: thanks team. they've accepted the rollback and want an incident summary and ETA on the config CI fix. Will escalate if any reoccurrence.

eli-ml: assigning action items: sam-eng -> add gating + feature flag default off. devon-sre -> automate KV safety cache invalidation post-config-deploy. jordan-cs -> customer postmortem. I'll run the regression harness and attach results.

jordan-cs: thanks everyone. tagging @acme-support: posting the interim postmortem in 1-2 hours. :thumbsup:

acme-support: appreciate the quick turnaround. will keep monitoring and report any anomalies.
